fields.name: SPI_WR_BIT_ORDER
fields.bit_confidence: high (matched via diagram divider lines + field label)
fields.description: This bit determines the bit order for command, address and data in transmitted signal. 1: sends LSB first; 0: sends MSB first. (R/W)

fields.name: SPI_RD_BIT_ORDER
fields.bit_confidence: high (matched via diagram divider lines + field label)
fields.description: This bit determines the bit order for received data in received signal. 1: re- ceives LSB first; 0: receives MSB first. (R/W)

fields.name: SPI_FREAD_DIO

fields.name: SPI_WP

fields.name: SPI_FREAD_QUAD

fields.name: SPI_MOSI_DELAY_NUM
fields.bit_confidence: high (matched via diagram divider lines + field label)
fields.description: It is used to configure the number of system clock cycles by which the MOSI signals are delayed. (R/W)

fields.name: SPI_MOSI_DELAY_MODE
fields.bit_confidence: high (matched via diagram divider lines + field label)
fields.description: This register field determines the way the MOSI signals are delayed by SPI clock. (R/W) After being delayed by SPI_MOSI_DELAY_NUM system clocks, the MOSI signals will then be delayed by the configuration of SPI_MOSI_DELAY_MODE, specifically: 0: no delay. 1: if SPI_CK_OUT_EDGE or SPI_CK_I_EDGE is set, the MOSI signals are delayed by half a cycle, otherwise they are delayed by one cycle. 2: if SPI_CK_OUT_EDGE or SPI_CK_I_EDGE is set, the MOSI signals are delayed by one cycle, otherwise they are delayed by half a cycle. 3: the MOSI signals are delayed one cycle.

fields.name: SPI_MISO_DELAY_NUM
fields.bit_confidence: high (matched via diagram divider lines + field label)
fields.description: It is used to configure the number of system clock cycles by which the MISO signals are delayed. (R/W)

fields.name: SPI_MISO_DELAY_MODE
fields.bit_confidence: high (matched via diagram divider lines + field label)
fields.description: This register field determines the way MISO signals are delayed by SPI clock. (R/W) After being delayed by SPI_MISO_DELAY_NUM system clock, the MISO signals will then be de- layed by the configuration of SPI_MISO_DELAY_MODE, specifically: 0: no delay. 1: if SPI_CK_OUT_EDGE or SPI_CK_I_EDGE is set, the MISO signals are delayed by half a cycle, otherwise they are delayed by one cycle. 2: if SPI_CK_OUT_EDGE or SPI_CK_I_EDGE is set, the MISO signals are delayed by one cycle, otherwise they are delayed by half a cycle. 3: the MISO signals are delayed by one cycle.

fields.name: SPI_HOLD_TIME
fields.bit_confidence: high (matched via diagram divider lines + field label)
fields.description: The number of SPI clock cycles by which CS pin signals are delayed. It is only valid when SPI_CS_HOLD is set to 1. (R/W)

fields.name: SPI_SETUP_TIME
fields.bit_confidence: high (matched via diagram divider lines + field label)
fields.description: It is to configure the time between the CS signal active edge and the first SPI clock edge. It is only valid in half-duplex mode or QSPI mode and when SPI_CS_SETUP is set to 1. registers.name: SPI_USER_REG

fields.name: SPI_CS_SETUP
fields.bit_confidence: high (matched via diagram divider lines + field label)
fields.description: Setting this bit enables a delay between CS active edge and the first clock edge, in multiples of one SPI clock cycle. In full-duplex mode and QSPI mode, setting this bit results in (SPI_SETUP_TIME + 1.5) SPI clock cycles delay. In full-duplex mode, there will be 1.5 SPI clock cycles delay for mode0 and mode2, and 1 SPI clock cycle delay for mode1 and mode3. (R/W)

fields.name: SPI_CS_HOLD

global_dependencies: Clock gate: DPORT_SPI01_CLK_EN (SPI0+SPI1 shared bit), DPORT_SPI2_CLK_EN (SPI2/HSPI), DPORT_SPI3_CLK_EN (SPI3/VSPI) in DPORT_PERIP_CLK_EN_REG (0x3FF000C0).
DPORT_SPI_DMA_CLK_EN gates the shared SPI DMA engine used by SPI1-3 in DMA mode.

SPI0 and SPI1 are reserved for accessing external flash/PSRAM by the system and should generally not be reconfigured by application code; SPI2 (HSPI) and SPI3 (VSPI) are the general-purpose controllers.
SPI_CLOCK_REG must be configured to set the clock divider before SPI_CMD_REG.SPI_USR is set to start a transaction.
SPI pins must be routed through the GPIO Matrix or IO_MUX before physical signaling occurs (see Chapter 6).
